headline: Intel's role in Elon Musk's Terafab chip plant stands after the TSMC talks, with Musk saying his own companies will build and run the site.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a new statement from Musk narrows an earlier talks story, but deal terms are undisclosed.
importance_line: It decides who will make chips for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, but Intel's financial terms, any TSMC sublease and how two rival chipmakers could share one campus are all unresolved.
summary: eeNews Europe reports that Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan confirmed on 7 Oct 2026 that Intel's deal on Terafab, Musk's planned chip factory in Grimes County, Texas for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, remains in place, while Musk said TSMC will not take control and that his companies will build and operate it, with TSMC possibly leasing part of the site. In our 4 Oct 2026 edition we carried Tom's Hardware's report that TSMC was in talks to join the project; no TSMC agreement has been announced, and Intel's commercial terms remain undisclosed.
notes: Follow-up of 1007:X16 (Bloomberg: Intel keeps working on Terafab) and of item 36 in the 4 Oct 2026 edition (TSMC talks, Tom's Hardware citing Culpium). New today: Musk's statement that his companies will operate the site. Full text read.
